messages.content: Ongoing: RoboRide drops price to $0.12 per mile. Wait time now 8 minutes. Coverage expanded to residential areas. Partnership wit
You notice more robotaxis on the streets. About 7% of people seem to be using them regularly.
Auto sector revenue index: 79 (baseline: 100). Foot traffic and sales are somewhat down.
People around you are stressed: Rick Tanner, Angela Wright. The mood is tense.

Howard closed the RoboRide file cleanly this week — updated inventory logs, moved the reserved brake consumables and sensors back to active stock, and called Carlos Ruiz directly. Carlos responded the same day with a $650 purchase order for brake pad sets, hybrid battery diagnostic connectors, and high-voltage insulated gloves, confirming the B2B reallocation is immediately productive. Angela Wright picked up on the first ring; Howard left the call with a written one-page job description in Angela's intake queue and a verbal commitment that she would prioritize displaced Hawkins counter-experience candidates for his part-time opening. Mark Thompson call happened Thursday — Howard acknowledged the delay, confirmed the educator discount on EV and hybrid consumables in writing via email, and got two names from Mark's vocational network as potential part-time counter candidates. The storefront window sign and social media post went up Friday afternoon. The monthly burn continues at -$2,780 net, partially offset by the Carlos order, for a net savings delta of -$2,130 — the best performing tick in four months.
